# Research notes: John 6:1–24

**What I couldn't find.** I ran out of searches before I could get to netbible.org, bibleodyssey.org, oca.org, the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org), the Pentecostal sites other than Enduring Word, and seedbed.com. So there are no notes below from those sources, and none for an Orthodox or Lutheran reading. I also found nothing on these verses from prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teachers. My notes on verses 16–18 and 22–24 are thinner than the rest.

---

**v. 1**
- **"Sea of Tiberias":** Ellicott says Jesus crossed from Galilee to the east side of the lake. He thinks "Tiberias" may have been added for Greek readers. The town was built by Herod and named after the Emperor Tiberius. That may explain why the name doesn't appear in the other Gospels. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **Which shore:** Hendriksen says readers who knew the earlier Gospel accounts would take "the other side" to mean the east (or north-east) of the sea. https://www.monergism.com/reformed-commentary-john-6
- **Why John tells this miracle at all:** Ellicott says John includes this Galilean miracle because of the teaching that follows it. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm

**v. 2**
- **The crowd kept coming:** Guzik quotes Morris: the Greek verbs mean the crowd "kept following" because they "continually saw" the signs Jesus "habitually did." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Why so many came:** Ellicott gives three reasons:
  - John the Baptist had just been killed, and his followers were turning to Jesus.
  - The Twelve had just come back from their mission.
  - Passover pilgrims were travelling the caravan road on the east side of the lake.
  
  https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm

**v. 3**
- **"The mountain":** Ellicott takes this as the hill country on the east shore. Guzik quotes Bruce, who identifies it as what is now the Golan Heights. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm; https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **The exact spot:** Coffman places the feeding on the plain of Butaiha, a mile or two to the east of Bethsaida. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/john-6.html

**v. 4**
- **Why Passover matters:** Ellicott says the Passover note is "not simply a note of time." It is a key to understanding both the miracle and the teaching that follows. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **The Exodus link:** Guzik notes that only John mentions Passover. The feast recalls God feeding Israel in the wilderness. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **A year before the cross:** Bengel says this Passover came Preceding His passion by the interval of a year. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/6-5.htm

**v. 5**
- **Why ask Philip? Answers differ:**
  - Gill and Benson: Philip came from Bethsaida and knew the area. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/6-5.htm
  - The Cambridge Bible lists several possibilities and says Any or all of these suggestions may be correct. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/6-5.htm
  - The Pulpit Commentary rejects Bengel's idea that Philip looked after the food, since Judas kept the money. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/john/6.htm
- **How this fits the other Gospels:** In the other Gospels the disciples raise the problem. Here Jesus does. Ellicott calls this different from, but not opposed to the other accounts. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm

**v. 6**
- **The traditional reading:** Jesus was testing Philip to train him, not to get information.
  - Constable calls it a test in Philip's discipleship training. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/6-5.html
  - Bible Hub's study notes put it as not for information but for formation. https://biblehub.com/john/6-5.htm
- **"Test" versus "tempt":** The Pulpit Commentary says this was a trial, not a temptation. God tests so that a person will succeed. The devil tempts hoping the person will fail. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/john/6.htm
- **A dissenting view (Meyer):** Meyer argues the word does not signify the trial of faith (so usually, even Hengstenberg). In his view it tested only whether Philip could come up with a practical plan. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/6-5.htm
- **A Methodist voice (Benson):** Jesus wanted to try what idea he had conceived of his divine power. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/6-5.htm
- **Augustine:** Jesus asked something He already knew in order to show the disciple's ignorance. Augustine thinks this also pointed to something deeper. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701024.htm

**v. 7**
- **What 200 denarii means:** Guzik calls it more than six months' wages. Philip's figures were accurate but no help in solving the problem. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Ellicott:** Philip had dwelt on the greatness of the need and had not learned the lessons of earlier miracles. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **Philip's sum was right:** Precept Austin cites a calculation showing that 200 denarii of barley would feed the men but not the women and children too. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary

**v. 8**
- **Andrew bringing people again:** Guzik notes Andrew once more brings someone to Jesus, as he brought Peter in 1:40–42. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Andrew and Philip together:** Ellicott says the two are linked here, in 12:22, and in the lists of the apostles. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm

**v. 9**
- **Barley loaves:** Ellicott calls them the ordinary black bread of Galilean peasants. Guzik says barley was simple food, often fed to animals, and suggests the boy was poor. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm; https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **The small words:** Ellicott says Andrew's remark, with its diminutive words, stresses the smallness of their power to help. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **The fish:** John MacArthur says the fish typically they would be pickled for preservation. https://www.gty.org/library/sermons-library/43-32/jesus-feeds-the-multitudes
- **Augustine's symbolic reading (Catholic and patristic):** by the five loaves are understood the five books of Moses. They are barley because they belong to the Old Testament. He sees the boy as perhaps Israel, and the two fish as priest and ruler. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701024.htm

**v. 10**
- **Order and the Shepherd:** Guzik sees Jesus acting in an orderly way, like the shepherd of Psalm 23 making people lie down in green pastures. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Spring grass:** Ellicott ties the grass to Passover, about April. "Men" means males, and Matthew adds that women and children were there as well. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **The real total:** Precept Austin estimates probably 10-15,000. MacArthur says between twenty and twenty-five thousand people. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary; https://www.gty.org/library/sermons-library/43-32/jesus-feeds-the-multitudes

**v. 11**
- **Where the miracle happened:** Bob Utley at bible.org says it must have occurred in Jesus' hands. Constable says Jesus multiplied the food as he broke it apart and distributed it. https://bible.org/book/export/html/19299; https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/6-11.html
- **Giving thanks:** Matthew Henry says we should give thanks for food even when it is "coarse and scanty." Gill says Jesus did it as His usual practice and as an example to us. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/6-11.html
- **Creation, not sharing:** Ryle says Food was called into existence that did not exist before. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ryl/john-6.html
- **Where readings differ: does this point to the Eucharist (the Lord's Supper)?**
  - *Catholic:* Catholic Answers quotes the Catechism (CCC 1335): the multiplied loaves prefigure the superabundance of this unique bread of his Eucharist. https://www.catholic.com/qa/was-jesus-feeding-of-the-5000-really-a-miracle-of-sharing
  - *Evangelical (Utley):* He notes that the Greek word for giving thanks later became the name for the Lord's Supper. But he also suggests John may have been reacting to the sacramental view. https://bible.org/book/export/html/19299
  - *Pulpit Commentary:* It mentions that some critics treat the story as a "glorification of the Eucharistial meal." The commentary itself does not adopt that view. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/john-6.html
- **Calvin (Reformed):** The crowd had to make do with barley bread and plain fish. Yet Christ does not cease to feed the whole world in a wonderful manner. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/6-11.html

**v. 12**
- **"They were full" proves the miracle:** Ryle argues the miracle was real: It would be impossible to convince five thousand hungry men in a wilderness that they were really filled, if they were not. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ryl/john-6.html
- **Jesus gave the order:** Ellicott notes that only John tells us the gathering was Jesus' own command. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **No waste:** Guzik says Jesus was "generous, but never wasteful." Precept Austin puts it as Abundance is no justification for waste. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/; https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary

**v. 13**
- **Why twelve baskets? Readings differ:**
  - *John Piper (Baptist):* The number is no mere coincidence, since Jesus calls His disciples "the Twelve." The leftovers were for the servers. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/twelve-baskets-of-bread-and-the-walk-on-water; https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-loving-meaning-of-the-leftovers
  - *Augustine:* The twelve baskets are the twelve Apostles, who themselves too were filled with the fragments of the Law. https://www.ccel.org/ccel/schaff/npnf106.vii.lxxxii.html

**v. 14**
- **"The Prophet":** Benson links the title to the Prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18. He takes it to mean the Messiah. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/6-5.htm
- **Moses and manna:** Guzik says the crowd made the Moses link, and the manna link with it. He warns that we too can love Jesus only for what He gives. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Elisha:** Barton (in Precept Austin) compares Elisha feeding 100 men with 20 loaves (2 Kings 4:42–44). https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary

**v. 15**
- **Why Jesus withdrew:** Ellicott says Matthew and Mark only tell us He went off to pray. John tells us why: He was avoiding a crowd that wanted a political Messiah. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm
- **A temptation refused:** Guzik quotes Morris, who calls an earthly kingdom a temptation from the devil, and Boice, who says the crowd hoped to use Jesus against Rome. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/

**v. 16**
- **"Went down":** Precept Austin says this shows the disciples had been on high ground. Matthew 14:22 adds that Jesus made them get into the boat. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary
- **Lesson, then test:** Constable says The feeding of the 5,000 was a lesson, and Jesus' walking on the water was the test following the lesson. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary

**v. 17**
- **Capernaum or Bethsaida?** John says the boat headed for Capernaum, but Mark 6:45 says Bethsaida. Hendriksen's answer is that this was another Bethsaida, situated somewhere in the vicinity of Capernaum. https://www.monergism.com/reformed-commentary-john-6

**vv. 18–19**
- **Divine power over the sea:** R.C. Sproul's Ligonier devotional says the disciples saw on this occasion a glimpse of Jesus' deity. To ancient Jews the sea was something only God could tame. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/walking-on-the-sea-of-galilee
- **Really on the water:** The Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary says Jesus was walking upon the sea," not just near or on land. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/john-6.html

**v. 20 — where readings really differ: "It is I" (Greek *egō eimi*)**
- **Read as God's name, "I AM":**
  - *Reformed (Ligonier):* It is a particularly strong hint at our Lord's deity. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/walking-on-the-sea-of-galilee
  - *Baptist (Garner-Howes):* It renders the phrase as "the self-existing one," linking it to Isaiah 43:1–2. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/john-6.html
  - *Catholic (Catholic Answers):* It connects the phrase with the burning bush in Exodus 3:14. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/online-edition/the-divinity-of-jesus-according-to-mark
- **Read as simple self-identification:**
  - Guzik quotes Bruce: here the words simply mean 'It is I'. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
  - Constable agrees that here Jesus was simply identifying Himself. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/6-20.html
- **Calvin:** Christ's presence alone gives calm and confidence. But the same words strike the wicked down in John 18:6. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/6-20.html

**v. 21**
- **"Willing":** Guzik takes it to mean Jesus waited to be welcomed into the boat. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Did the boat arrive miraculously?**
  - Ligonier says it may suggest a miracle of some kind, but leaves the question open. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/walking-on-the-sea-of-galilee
  - Guzik quotes an older writer who thought the boat moved on its own the rest of the way. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Piper:** Jesus himself came to them. The gift here is His presence, not more bread. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/twelve-baskets-of-bread-and-the-walk-on-water

**vv. 22–23**
- **Timing:** Hendriksen dates this to the morning after the feeding, when Jesus had already landed on the western shore. https://www.monergism.com/reformed-commentary-john-6
- **What the crowd worked out:** Guzik says they had seen the disciples leave without Jesus. Now they noticed He was gone too. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-6/
- **Tiberias:** Ellicott says the town of Tiberias is named in the New Testament only here. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/john/6.htm

**v. 24**
- **Not the whole crowd:** Ryle says this need not mean all five thousand. Most had probably gone home or on to Jerusalem for Passover. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ryl/john-6.html
- **The wrong motive:** Hendriksen says Jesus then criticized their thoroughly materialistic motive in seeking him. https://www.monergism.com/reformed-commentary-john-6

---

**Debated modern teaching: the "miracle of sharing"**
Some modern readers explain the feeding as people simply sharing their own lunches. Two sources I read reject this:
- Catholic Answers says it was not a "miracle of sharing" or anything similar to that. https://www.catholic.com/qa/was-jesus-feeding-of-the-5000-really-a-miracle-of-sharing
- Precept Austin says it was not people finding lunches in the crowd: Such suggestions are without foundation. https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-6-commentary
